Ercoform in the field

Shape the protection to the actual channel.

Ercoform is fabricated for the project, positioned across the prepared site and filled with structural grout in place. These examples show how the system can be fitted across different channel geometries while protecting the bed, side slopes and nearby infrastructure.

Channel and crossing protection

Protect the flow path around critical infrastructure.

The channel and side slopes are rebuilt around the crossing, then protected with a continuous mat formed to the site.

Localized channel stabilization

Fit the protection to an irregular site.

Custom-fabricated panels follow the reconstructed channel limits and are completed in place as an integrated protective system.

How Ercoform works

A strong system that can still move.

Ercoform begins as a dual-layer woven fabric form that is sewn to the dimensions and configuration established by the project design. High-strength tendons and revetment cables connect the individual grout-filled blocks into a continuous mattress.

Once the prepared site is ready, the custom panels are positioned, connected and filled with structural grout. The finished system provides substantial protection while retaining the ability to conform and articulate rather than behaving like a single rigid slab.

  1. Evaluate and Design

    Understand the erosion mechanism, site geometry, field conditions and assets at risk.

  2. Fabricate for the Site

    Sew the mat system to match the project-specific design before mobilization.

  3. Position and Connect

    Place the panels on the prepared area and assemble them according to the construction drawings.

  4. Pump and Finish

    Fill the forms with structural grout, complete anchoring and restore the surrounding site.

Why site-specific matters

The product is shaped by the problem.

Conforms to Geometry

Panels are configured around the actual channel, bank and infrastructure rather than forcing the site to fit a standard product.

Supports Constructability

The design accounts for access, preparation, anchoring, placement and how the work will be executed in the field.

Adapts to the Site

The connected mat can conform to prepared contours and accommodate changing field conditions.

Plans Beyond Today

The design can account for anticipated bottom and side-slope degradation, not only the damage visible during evaluation.

The goal is not an online diagnosis

It is a better first conversation.
